note: Documented lifecycle capability flags transcribed from each vendor's own documentation on the checked_at date. Flags describe what the documentation claims, not what was measured here. Any flag may change; re-check the linked page before relying on it.

corrections.reason: Transcription error, not a page change. The checked page states filesystem-only snapshots explicitly; the earlier value contradicted the source sentence recorded in research/evidence/e2b-vs-daytona-vs-blaxel-2026/e2b-persistence.md.

documented_notes: By default a pause saves both the filesystem and the memory. To save only the filesystem - a lighter snapshot that reboots on resume - pass mode: filesystem (also onTimeout {action: pause, mode: filesystem}).
Pause/resume preserves filesystem and memory, including running processes and loaded variables.
A paused sandbox is kept indefinitely with no automatic deletion until explicitly killed.
Continuous runtime window is 24 hours on Pro and 1 hour on Hobby; pausing resets the window.
On timeout the sandbox can automatically pause to preserve state instead of being killed.
Pause/resume is not listed as supported for Container sandboxes.
Archive is Container-only; archived state stores the filesystem in object storage.
A stopped Container sandbox keeps its filesystem on the runner.
Pause/resume is supported for Linux VM and Windows sandboxes; a paused VM keeps filesystem and memory state offloaded to nearby storage.
Archive is not listed as supported for VM sandboxes.
Filesystem-plus-memory snapshots and forking are supported for VM sandboxes.
Same lifecycle row as Linux VM in the vendor capability matrix.
Archive is not listed as supported for VM sandboxes.
Neither pause/resume nor archive is listed as supported for GPU sandboxes.
Filesystem-only snapshots are supported; filesystem-plus-memory snapshots are not.
Standby snapshots the full state, files and running processes included; sandboxes wait on standby indefinitely.
The standby transition happens in approximately 15 seconds after the last active connection; an idle WebSocket/TCP connection has a 15-minute idle timeout.
Memory is not charged in standby; snapshot and/or volume storage is charged.
Archive is a separate lifecycle: it stores filesystem changes over the image, does not preserve memory, and restarts processes on unarchive.
